articleTitle: Underwater wireless optical communications: From system-level demonstrations to channel modelling
abstract: In this paper, we discuss about recent experimental advances in underwater wireless optical communications (UWOC) over various underwater channel water types using different modulation schemes as well as modelling and describing the statistical properties of turbulence-induced fading in underwater wireless optical channels using laser beam intensity fluctuations measurements.

articleTitle: Design of 100Gbps double transverse coupled cavity VCSELs
abstract: We present a novel design of double-transverse-coupled-cavity VCSELs toward ultrahigh speed modulations of 100Gbps. In-plane lateral optical feedback in both cavities enables the large bandwidth enhancement of direct modulations. Clear eye opening can be observed up to 100Gbps and the frequency chirp is reduced by a factor more than two.

articleTitle: High extinction ratio LN modulator with low half-wave voltage and small chirp by using thin substrate
abstract: We investigate the characteristics of LN modulator using thin substrate in both calculation and experiment. The fabricated active Y-branch integrated Mach-Zehnder modulator using thin LN substrate showed a good performance such as low half-wave voltage of 1.23 V, small chirp parameter of 0.013, and high extinction ratio of 44 dB.

articleTitle: Boronic acid-functionalized magnetic nanocomposites for an efficient extraction of dopamine molecules and their detection using fluorescent polydopamine
abstract: Drug-induced dyskinesia is caused by dopamine receptor blockers, drugs prescribed for treatment such as depression and insomnia in clinical practice. It is necessary to have a reliable and facile technique which can quantify the dopamine concentration in real time. We have prepared boronic acid-functionalized magnetic nanocomposites which can capture plasma dopamine and its detection using fluorescent polydopamine.

articleTitle: Proposal of Si-based integrated probe for laser Doppler cross-sectional velocity distribution measurement
abstract: A Si-based integrated probe is proposed for cross-sectional velocity distribution measurements. The measuring principle is based on a combination of simultaneous multipoint measurement using spatial encoding and nonmechanical scanning. The scanning function of the probe employing chirped focusing grating couplers in the transmitting optics is simulated.

articleTitle: Light-induced self-written waveguide formation by near-infrared wavelength continuous wave laser light
abstract: We evaluated one-photon absorption light-induced self-written (1PA-LISW) waveguide formation using near-infrared wavelength continuous wave (CW) laser light. It offers an alternative approach to the conventional optical interconnection method that requires two-photon absorption polymerization using a high-power pulse laser. We used a combination of diimonium dye and a CW laser light with a wavelength around 1070 nm through a fiber to form the LISW waveguide. A waveguide core of maximum length of 1 mm was realized based on 1PA-LISW process.

articleTitle: Optical communications for next generation automotive networks
abstract: The next-generation cars require high speed on-board communication networks. The latest amendment to IEEE 802.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TM</sup> specifies a gigabit plastic optical fiber-based communication standard for automotive. New use cases, where optical communications are the most suitable choice, are described along with OEM's requirements for multi-gigabit future standards.

articleTitle: Proposal of signal processing based on machine learning in Brillouin optical correlation domain analysis/ reflectometry
abstract: We proposed the signal processing based on machine learning in Brillouin optical correlation domain analysis/reflectometry (BOCDA/R). The methodology of the new idea is illustrated in this paper. The machine learning method is expected to perform more reliable and efficient than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Observation of eigenmode propagation in few-mode fibers by selective LP mode excitation
abstract: We observed near-field patterns of output light from few-mode fibers in which an LP mode was selectively excited. It is revealed from the variation of intensity profile against wavelength change that eigenmodes of circular core are supported in single core FMFs while LP modes are guided in a multicore FMF.

articleTitle: Fundamental demonstration of mode-group demultiplexing technique based on volume holographic demultiplexer
abstract: We demonstrated the mode-group demultiplexing technique based on a volume holographic demultiplexer (VHDM) for mode-group division multiplexing transmission using multi-mode fibers. In the experiment, the VHDM achieved the separating of three mode-group channels with a single holographic recording medium. Thus, the modal cross-talk was obtained as −14.7 dB.

articleTitle: VCSEL technology for imaging and sensor systems applications
abstract: Vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser diodes (VCSELs) provide extraordinary properties like sub-mA threshold current, multi-GHz modulation capability, or relative intensity noise close to the quantum limit. VCSELs have become a preferred light source for optical sensor technologies and imaging systems. The purpose is to review some recent developments with special attention to mass market employments and to reveal future applications.

articleTitle: Consideration of wall-plug efficiency for LEDs
abstract: LED characteristics for the situation wherein the wall-plug efficiency exceeds unity was investigated. Availability of such device leads to a possibility of energy harvesting system by combining LED and PD. However, the resulting system becomes a perpetual motion machine, which should not be available. This puzzling problem is discussed.

articleTitle: Non-destructive inspection of semiconductor optical waveguide using optical coherence tomography with visible broadband light source
abstract: Non-destructive inspection of semiconductor optical waveguides was demonstrated using optical coherence tomography with a visible broadband light source (vis-OCT). Comparisons of measured height and width between the vis-OCT, stylus profiler, and cross-sectional scanning electron microscopy indicated the effectiveness of the vis-OCT as a high-resolution, non-destructive, and non-contact measurement method.

articleTitle: Output position variation in grating coupler integrated in waveguide resonator
abstract: Grating coupler (GC) in waveguide cavity resonator can provide high-efficiency vertical coupling with small aperture. Coupling efficiency of GC depends on waveguide resonator shift. Output position variation is theoretically predicted and experimentally demonstrated. Devices were fabricated in a Si-N waveguide on a SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> substrate for operating at 1.55 μm.

articleTitle: Breakdown voltage based transformer oil analysis using optical fiber as sensor
abstract: A new physical model considering polymer optical fiber as a sensor for quality analysis of transformer oil based on the breakdown voltage of transformer oil is proposed. The quality of transformer oil is analyzed based on the estimated data from the proposed system and result obtained from the conventional breakdown voltage (BDV) test. The measurement of BDV based on the sensor output voltage indicates the condition of the oil samples.

articleTitle: Au nanostructures electrodeposited on graphene oxide-modified ITO glass as SERS substrates for dopamine detection in human serum
abstract: Surface enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is one of the best analytical tools which can identify probing molecules with an ultralow concentration. As a sensitive SERS substrate, we electrodeposited Au nanostructures on the ITO glass modified with graphene oxide, in order to detect the dopamine (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−8</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−9</sup> M) in human serum.

articleTitle: Independent drive of integrated multicolor (RGBY) micro-LED array using regularly arrayed InGaN based nanocolumns
abstract: We demonstrate monolithic integration of blue-, green-, yellow-, and red-emitting micro light emitting diodes (LEDs) and their independent drive using matrix wiring electrodes. The four-color (RGBY) micro-LEDs are prepared on the same template by using regularly arrayed InGaN based nanocolumns with different column diameters and periods via selective area growth.

articleTitle: 60 GHz band optical single-sideband modulator using polarization-reversed structures with asymmetric Mach-Zehnder optical waveguide
abstract: We have proposed a new optical single-sideband (SSB) modulator using polarization-reversed structures for 60 GHz band radio-over-fiber systems, which enables us to have the SSB optical modulation without an external power supply. The SSB modulation characteristics and the switching of enhanced side-bands were successfully demonstrated in the 60 GHz band.

articleTitle: Mach-Zehnder interferometer with Fabry-Perot cavities in silicon-on-insulator for biosensing
abstract: We demonstrate a Fabry-Perot cavity based on Bragg grating mirrors in both arms of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer. The devices were fabricated in silicon-on-insulator and are useful for characterizing the waveguide parameters and obtaining a highly precise and sensitive sensor with a temperature compensating scheme.

articleTitle: Efficiency improvement by serial-connection of VCSEL array for optical wireless power transmission
abstract: A high power - series connected vertical cavity surface emitting laser array module for optical wireless power transmission was investigated. Series connection is advantageous for improving efficiency and freedom of system design. Numerical analysis showed a large effect of series connection. Fabricated prototype module showed increased efficiency.

articleTitle: Fiber optic interconnection devices for in-vehicle communication
abstract: In-vehicle optical communication has a 20-year history. This paper introduces the trends and future applications focusing on interconnection devices and related international standards. Cost competitive fiber optic solutions against copper solutions are the expected technology to realize electromagnetic interference-free high-data rate communication for achieving autonomous driving systems in the future.

articleTitle: AC magnetic field imaging by using digital micro-mirror device
abstract: We demonstrated optical imagings of AC magnetic fields. A digital micro-mirror device and a lock-in detection allowed obtaining sub-millimeter resolution images without using magnetic shields. Images of gradient field from a wire suggested its potential to apply for signal-source estimations.

articleTitle: Efficient silicon nitride grating coupler with a dielectric multilayer reflector
abstract: A highly efficient grating coupler with a dielectric multilayer reflector for silicon nitride photonic integrated circuits was proposed. Design, fabrication and optical characterization were presented. The peak coupling efficiency and 3 dB bandwidth are -4.5 dB and 68.0 nm, respectively. The fabrication process is CMOS-compatible with only one etching step.

articleTitle: Fast wavelength stabilization of tunable laser after starting laser oscillation
abstract: For fast wavelength switching within the full available wavelength range of the tunable laser array, we investigated a wavelength stabilizing method after switching on the injection current to the laser's active layer. Experimental results demonstrated that our feedback controller dramatically reduced wavelength switching time from 800 μs to 2.0 μs.

articleTitle: Proposal of interference signal processing for dynamic displacement measurement with high time-resolution
abstract: We present a laser interference measurement method to monitor the transient motion of an object taking place within 1 μs. We propose a novel interference signal processing as a key technology, and confirm the capability of 2.5-ns time resolution.

articleTitle: Design of a high-speed graphene optical modulator on a silicon slot waveguide
abstract: In this paper, we propose a way to utilize the silicon slot waveguide structure to create a high speed, low power consumption and low insertion loss graphene optical modulator. The active region of the modulator is assumed to be a two graphene layer capacitor structure and the proposal is supported by numerical simulations of absorption.

articleTitle: Electromagnetically-induced focusing controlled by a microwave field
abstract: We have theoretically predicted the effect of a microwave field on cross-focusing of an optical weak probe beam by a copropagating non-uniform control beam in an electromagnetically-induced transparency medium. Our numerical simulation shows probe beam focusing about 30% of its initial width in absence of microwave, whereas it focuses 70% in presence of microwave field.

articleTitle: Multiple photon photon resonance by using active-multimode interferometer laser diode
abstract: Active-multimode interferometer laser diode that integrates at least six oscillating cavities has been achieved successfully. Multiple cavities contribute to multiple longitudinal mode spacings as well as multiple PPR frequencies. Device aiming 100 GHz bandwidth design principle is proposed.

articleTitle: Novel fiber attachment techniques for miniaturization of planar lightwave circuit module
abstract: Micro planar lightwave circuit modules with practical strength were fabricated by novel fiber attachment techniques using capillaries and glass films. In a damp heat storage test at 85°C and 85% RH, the loss increase was less than 1.0 dB after 2000 hours at a wavelength of 636 nm.

articleTitle: Silicon photonics for optical computing, interconnects and sensing
abstract: Silicon photonics has been an active research topic for the past twenty years. The maturity of silicon nanofabrication and the transparency of silicon material at C- and L-band are a critical factor for the realization of silicon photonics for real applications. However, due to the intrinsic nature of indirect bandgap, hybrid integration with external III-V based lasers is the trend for integration. In this talk, we will focus on several key application areas. Figure 1 shows the system architecture to be demonstrated using III-V and silicon integrated photonic devices where energy consumption and bandwidth can be significantly improved.

articleTitle: Gold and silver core-shell nanoparticles for light absorption enhancement of organic solar cells
abstract: To increase light absorption without altering the thickness of active layer for OPV, rough surface Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticle (RSAu@Ag NPs) was prepared. Direct incorporation of RSAu@Ag NPs at the bottom of active layer improved the light absorption because of scattering power and board spectral response of Au NPs.

articleTitle: Silicon photonics for optical communication and sensing
abstract: Silicon photonic integrated circuits, the guiding of light in silicon waveguides clad in oxide, are primarily used for fiberoptic communication and optical sensing. Their high yield, low cost, small footprint, polarization-handling capability, silicon-industry foundries, and silicon-industry packaging allow bring tremendous advantages to complex systems, especially ones based on coherent detection.

articleTitle: Beam propagation analysis of optical activity and circular dichroism in helically twisted photonic crystal fiber
abstract: Transmission characteristics of helically twisted photonic crystal fiber is theoretically investigated by using recently developed beam propagation method for helicoidal system. Experimentally reported features of twisted PCF, such as periodical transmission dips, optical activity discontinuity, and circular dichroism are successfully reproduced in the simulation.

articleTitle: Heat-resistant low-loss connectors for gigabit plastic optical fiber communication
abstract: Withdrawal of plastic optical fiber from assembled ferrule at connections by thermal shock causes increase in connection loss, which becomes a problem for automotive gigabit optical communication. Our two proposals, an uptaperd ferrule and filling an refractive index matching member (Fit Well), showed positive results from -40°C to +105°C.

articleTitle: Pluggable photonic circuit platform using a novel passive alignment method
abstract: We propose a novel passive alignment method for multiple silica-based planar lightwave circuit (PLC) interconnections. The method employs grooves for fitting formed on a silica-based PLC with optical fibers. We achieved low-loss PLC interconnections with the method. The method is a promising way of realizing cost-effective and pluggable multi-PLC integration.

articleTitle: Weight sensor by 3D printed mechanically induced long-period fiber grating for power control inside single-mode fiber
abstract: 3D printed mechanically induced long-period fiber grating has been presented as a novel device for power attenuation inside a single-mode fiber. The perturbation of the device causes the coupling of fundamental core mode to cladding modes. The maximum power attenuates when the weight is perturbed.

articleTitle: A photonic crystal nanocavity with a quantum dot active region embedded by MBE regrowth
abstract: We fabricated a two dimensional photonic crystal nanocavity embedding a spatially-isolated active region containing InAs quantum dots using crystal regrowth with molecular beam epitaxy. We observed a cavity mode with a quality factor over 10,000, despite the existence of a mound structure on top of the buried active region due to faceting during the regrowth.

articleTitle: Proposal of cost-efficient and low-complexity platform for software defined visible light communication
abstract: With the increasing popularity of LED lighting and a growing demand for bandwidth in wireless communication, the visible light communication (VLC) is one of the promising scheme for addressing the bottleneck in the emerging broadband access networks. For research in the field of VLC focused on solutions of contradiction between massive available bandwidth and limited modulation bandwidth of LED, the purpose of this paper is to design an VLC experiment platform with characteristics of high flexibility and rapid productization. As a result, this platform not only expand the concept of software defined communication, but has the advantage of simple structure and low cost.

articleTitle: Laser rangefinders for planetary exploration
abstract: Laser rangefinders are often used as observation or navigation sensors for spacecraft. Here, this paper reports on lasers and receivers, which are important components in laser rangefinders.

articleTitle: Offset-launch measurement for few-mode long-period fiber gratings fabricated using tilted amplitude mask
abstract: Spectral measurements of long-period fiber gratings (LPGs) were performed with an offset launch for higher-order mode excitation. LPGs with various grating periods were fabricated with the tilted mask method. Difference in the attenuation peaks was observed for various offsets. The results were compared with simulation for LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> and LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> modes.

articleTitle: Medium-range propagation experiment using optical duplicate system
abstract: A compact and mobile optical duplicate system with two rectangular array lenses was designed for reducing the influence of atmospheric fluctuation on satellite-ground laser communication. A ray-trace simulation confirmed that this optical duplicate system satisfies the required conditions for the medium-range propagation experiment.

articleTitle: MEMS based micromirror arrays
abstract: MEMS micromirror arrays for active daylight guiding via smart windows have been implemented and characterized. Tailored lighting for users as well as energy saving in air conditioning and heating is envisaged. Recent experimental results on required electrostatic actuation voltages, extrapolated lifetime, power consumption and heat impact are presented.

articleTitle: Analyses of all-optical gate switches employing quasi-phase matched devices: Effects on pattern difference of domain inversion period error
abstract: We analyze characteristics of all-optical switches using the QPM devices with consideration for the value and the pattern difference of the random period error. The error must be reduced significantly for realizing proper switching operation.

articleTitle: On-chip Brillouin processing for coherent optical communications
abstract: We present our recent results on harnessing the nonlinear stimulated Brillouin scattering effect on a photonic chip for coherent optical communications. At the transmitter-end, an optical frequency comb was regenerated through on-chip Brillouin scattering for 64-level QAM communications. At the receiver-end, low-latency self-homodyne reception was achieved through Brillouin-assisted carrier recovery.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of a digital holographic microscope based on a planar lightwave circuit
abstract: We have developed a Digital Holographic Microscope based on a Planar Lightwave Circuit (PLC-DHM) that uses a spherical surface reference wave. This PLC-DHM is performed without any lenses for magnification of the object image. In this study, we evaluated the performance of this PLC-DHM system and measured bio samples.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental thermal resistance of VCSELs considering thermal conductivity reduction effect of thin layer
abstract: Reduction of thermal conductivity in a thin layer structure has been known, however the influence to the device has not been discussed clearly. This study analysed thermal resistance of VCSEL numerically and compared with experimentally fabricated device. The effect is significant influence which can not be ignored in device design.

articleTitle: Evaluation of wavelength dependence of integrated MZM using balanced-bridge and asymmetric X waveguide structures for high extinction ratio modulation
abstract: In this study, we measure the wavelength dependence on the device operation of integrated Mach-Zehnder modulators in cascade. We use a balanced-bridge and asymmetric X coupler. We investigate the extinction ratio and bias voltage of these structures, and calculate the relationship between the phase change and the imperfect-bias extinction ratio.

articleTitle: WDM lasers and arrays for applications in optical networking and interconnect: Overview and perspectives
abstract: The technologies to realize WDM laser arrays are addressed with focus on wavelength registration and manufacturing complexity. The challenges of applying the laser arrays in practical systems will be discussed. An application example to realize laser arrays for next-generation optical interconnect will be highlighted.

articleTitle: Silicon waveguide michelson interferometer for multi-wavelength modulator
abstract: A waveguide multi-wavelength modulator is investigated. The modulator is based on Michelson interferometer, which is composed of phase shifter and microring resonator wavelength filters, leading to respective wavelength arms. Multi-channel operation of Michelson interferometer switch is demonstrated using a thermo-optic phase shifter.

articleTitle: MOVPE growth of lattice matched InAs/GaAsSb superlattice on InAs substrate for mid-infrared sensing devices
abstract: We investigated the gas flow sequence to realize short period and lattice matched InAs/GaAsSb superlattice on InAs substrate by MOVPE. Arsenic composition of GaAsSb for lattice matching was adjusted by adding AsH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> flow to residual arsenic incorporation. Clear photoluminescence peak at 4 μm range was observed. This wavelength is attractive for CO and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas sensing applications.

articleTitle: Basic study on real-time vibration displacement measurement using probe light modulated by phase-modulated RF signal
abstract: We propose real-time vibration displacement measurement system using probe light modulated by phase-modulated RF signal. The reflected probe light is processed by a signal detection unit composed of an optical intensity modulator and lock-in amplifier. Proof-of-concept experiment demonstrates real-time measurement of 50-Hz vibration displacement with an amplitude of 21 mm.

articleTitle: Ultrafast direct measurement of HBT effect by two-photon absorption based on Feynman's path-integral theory
abstract: Hanbury Brown and Twiss effect of thermal light is directly observed in a modified Michelson interferometer with a two-photon absorption detector at the ultrafast timescale. The contribution of other items in signal of two-photon absorption detector are analyzed in detail by employing Feynman's path-integral theory.

articleTitle: Silicon waveguide TE0/TE1 mode conversion Bragg grating for constituting a resonator device
abstract: We report a mode conversion Bragg grating using silicon waveguide to attain strong diffraction. Grating structures using sidewall grating and photonic crystal type are described. By incorporating a resonator structure, a narrow transmission peak can be obtained. Structures for suppressing the unwanted diffraction into the same mode are also discussed.

articleTitle: VCSEL and microlens array: Parallel microoptics world
abstract: We review a new microoptics world based upon the idea of vertical cavity surface emitting laser (VCSEL) and 2D arrayed microlenses.

articleTitle: Photonics polymers for fiber and display
abstract: We have proposed and demonstrated the high-speed graded-index plastic optical fiber (GI POF) which will be “capillary of light” for consumers in 8K era. The zero-birefringent and super-birefringent polymer films are introduced for realizing real color display in LCD and OLED.

articleTitle: Magnetic field sensing by bi-layer Ni-based subwavelength periodic structure operating visible wavelength region
abstract: Magnetic field sensor with very simple normal light incident geometry was developed using bi-layer nickel-based subwavelength periodic structure. Peaks in refraction spectra from the fabricated nickel-subwavelength structure shifted considerably with increasing external magnetic field, owing to phase variation of eigenmode within the periodic structure for the field.

articleTitle: MEMS plasmonic switch with stripe plasmonic waveguide
abstract: We designed the new plasmonic switch that combines a stripe plasmonic waveguide and MEMS. On-off extinction ratio and mechanical modulation resonance frequency was numerically estimated to be 10 dB and 70 kHz, respectively. We confirmed the displacement of moving part depending on applied voltage.

articleTitle: A thickness-varying sub-wavelength grating focusing lens for TE polarization light
abstract: A focusing lens for TE polarization light based on silicon sub-wavelength gratings using two different thicknesses is proposed. The properties are numerically studied with Finite Element Method (FEM). Total transmissivity is 72% and the full-width-half-maximum (FWHM) at focal plane is 0.8μm at a wavelength of 1550nm.

articleTitle: Terahertz wave beam steering by optical phase control
abstract: We investigated the ability to tilt the terahertz wave beam at arrayed photomixers. Experimental demonstration showed that optical phase control enabled us to make a beam steering of a 300-GHz terahertz wave in a range of 25 degrees.

articleTitle: 32-Gbps modulation of single silicon microring resonator-loaded Mach-Zehnder modulator
abstract: Modulation characteristics of compact single silicon microring resonator-loaded Mach-Zehnder modulators (MRR-MZM) with different device parameters are discussed. 32-Gbps modulation at the driving voltage of 4 V is demonstrated in the MZM with a single Si MRR having a coupling efficiency of 0.15 and a round-trip length of 180 μm.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive fiber-optic refractive index sensor based on multimode interference with fiber-loop technique
abstract: We introduced a fiber-optic sensor, based on multimode interference, in a fiber-loop technique to realize ultrasensitive refractive index measurement. The multiplied interaction of multimode interference in the fiber-loop enlarged the spectral contrast, resulting in a sensitivity several tens of times higher than that of the sensor without the fiber-loop.

articleTitle: WDM coupler for signal and second harmonic pump based on silica-based PLC for hybrid integration of linear and nonlinear optical devices
abstract: We fabricated a low-loss wavelength division multi/demultiplexing coupler using silica-based planar lightwave circuits for hybrid integration with nonlinear optical waveguides as an advanced optical signal processing technology. We can use this coupler to multi/demultiplex 1.56- and 0.78-μm lights with low loss by modifying the gap distance of the directional coupler.

articleTitle: Low attenuation mode converter with modal power distribution controllability by twist processing in step-index optical fibers
abstract: We proposed a short-fiber-length mode scrambler that reproduces the equilibrium mode distribution of an A3e fiber. The mode scrambler is compact, mode-controllable and has low attenuation. It is effective for not only hard plastic-clad fiber but also all step-index fibers, such as all-glass and plastic optical fibers.

articleTitle: Proposal of quantum well polarization modulator based on double microring resonator for stokes vector modulation
abstract: A compact polarization modulator based on a multiple quantum well (MQW) Butterworth double microring resonator (MRR) is proposed. Owing to an enhanced phase shift in an MRR, the length of the modulator can be significantly reduced. Using polarization-dependent electrorefractive index change in the MQW, continuous polarization control can be realized.

articleTitle: Long-term stability improvement of Brillouin measurement in plastic optical fibers by fresnel suppression using amorphous fluoropolymer
abstract: For Brillouin-sensing applications, we develop a method of mitigating the Fresnel reflection at the end of perfluorinated plastic optical fibers by covering there with amorphous fluoropolymer (CYTOP; material of the fiber core) dissolved in volatile solvent. Even after the solvent evaporates, the CYTOP layer remains, leading to long-lasting Fresnel reduction.

articleTitle: Dual-wavelength, low-coherence digital holography using quantum dot based light source
abstract: The dual-wavelength digital holography with low-coherence light source by quantum dot film is proposed. By converting initial LED beam using QD film of different optical properties, practical 3D measurement system using dual-wavelength DH with only single LED could be obtained.

articleTitle: Comparison of wavefront coding optical system using two conjugate phase masks among cubic, sinusoidal, and tangent phase masks
abstract: Wavefront coding is an effective technique for extending the depth of field. We verified the usefulness of the method of generating symmetrical point spread function by using two conjugate phase masks. According to the results of this study, this method is effective at a small defocus.

articleTitle: Selective mode conversion using dual-phase modulation
abstract: We propose a selective mode conversion method using dual-phase modulation which performs the full-complex amplitude modulation by use of two phase-type spatial light modulators. In the experiment, the crosstalk to undesired spatial mode was supressed less than −21.2 dB for the 4-LP modes of a few-mode fiber.

articleTitle: Linearizer for wavelength sweep at tunable DBR-LD and linearity evaluation of sweep
abstract: We constructed the linear wavelength sweeping system with 2-μm-band distributed Bragg reflector laser for the second-harmonic-detection wavelength modulation spectroscopy. Using our devised linearity evaluation method with a germanium etalon filter, we experimentally confirmed that the nonlinearity of the laser can be efficiently compensated.

articleTitle: Tens-of-nanometer-scale dynamic displacement measurement using active change of operation point for phase modulator
abstract: In a tens-of-nanometer-scale dynamic displacement measurement system based on a fiber interferometer using high-frequency phase modulation for the reference light, we introduce active change of operation point for the phase modulator. It is experimentally demonstrated that dynamic displacement measurement is possible independent of the initial operation point.

articleTitle: Image evaluation based on the mean structural similarity for wavefront coding
abstract: We would like a numerical value that indicates the extent to which restoration is achieved compared with the original image in wavefront coding. Using the mean structural similarity (MSSIM) as the image evaluation value, we evaluated restored images and compared phase masks. In this study, we confirmed that it is desirable to optimize the coefficients of the phase mask so that the MSSIM is highest to obtain high-quality restored images.

articleTitle: Hybrid ultra thin silicon and electro-optic polymer waveguide modulator
abstract: Compact and, low driving voltage optical modulator is the key device for high-speed on-chip optical interconnects. We have fabricated a hybrid silicon and electro-optic (EO) polymer modulator and demonstrated its EO properties. We used thin silicon core and planar electrodes to enable the modulator a low driving voltage.

articleTitle: Output characteristics for high-order resonance modes in resonance-type guided-wave optical acoustic emission sensors
abstract: A resonance-type guided-wave optical acoustic emission (AE) sensor consists of a diaphragm and a single-mode optical waveguide. In order to increase detectable frequency, the feasibility of application of high-order resonance modes was examined by their measured output characteristics using acoustic pulses or continuous waves instead of AE pulses.

articleTitle: CAD modelling of optical fiber reflectance probe for biomedical diffuse reflectance spectroscopy applications
abstract: In this paper we present a CAD model of optical fibre reflectance probe for biomedical diffuse reflectance spectroscopy applications. Henyey-Greenstein model is used to model the scattering form the biomedical tissue. The CAD model is used to predict the coupling efficiency of the fibre probe with different multimode fibre core diameter and to estimate the separation distance between the probe and the sample for optimized coupling.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of GaN-based UVLEDs under forward bias operations in salty vapor environment
abstract: We illustrated the reliability of longer wavelength ultraviolet light-emitting diodes (UVLEDs) in salty vapour environment under manipulation of forward-bias stress via consistent electrical and material characterizations. By manipulating the unprecedented operation in salty vapour ambient, we investigated a series of remarkable findings related to origin of failure behaviours.

articleTitle: Preparation of Cu2O@apoferritin for detection of dopamine
abstract: Non-toxic Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O@apoferritin was prepared by employing CuCl<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and apoferritin. The morphology and structure of Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O@apoferritin were investigated by HR-TEM and XRD. The size of Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O nanoparticle was 2.5 nm and it was found that the photoluminescence of Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O QD@apoferritin could be used as a sensor media for detection of dopamine.

articleTitle: 50 Years of fibers and integrated optics
abstract: Research and development of fibers and integrated optics have a long history over a half century. The history is briefly reviewed and the recent progress of space and mode division mulplexing transmission using multi-core and few mode fibres is introduced focusing on the review of mode theory of optical fiber.

articleTitle: Highly aberrated phase elements for presbyopia and astigmatism correction
abstract: We propose the use of highly aberrated cubic phase elements for correction of presbyopia in combination with astigmatism. The experimental validation shows that it is possible to extend the range of clear vision from 0.6m to 6m for presbyopes with an astigmatism up to 2D regardless on the orientation of its axis.

articleTitle: Resonant frequency analysis of dielectric equilateral triangular microcavities
abstract: In this work, we analyse the resonant frequencies and fields of dielectric equilateral triangular resonators using the Muller boundary integral equations. The results are presented for both TE- and TM-modes and interpreted in terms of semiclassical physics.

articleTitle: New method for development of fused silica fibres with freeform nanostructured gradient index core
abstract: We present a new type of gradient index fused silica fibre with nanostructured core. A gradient index core is obtained by means of arbitrary distribution of two types of subwavelength glass rods. The proposed method allows to obtain arbitrary gradient distribution not limited to a circular symmetry as in standard gradient index fibers. We have developed a proof of concept fibre and show a very good match between design and the measured properties of the fibre.

articleTitle: Progress in quantum dots for advanced photonics
abstract: Since the first proposal of quantum dot in 1982, the quantum dots have been intensively investigated for both fundamental solid state physics and application to advanced photonic devices. In this presentation, we overview progress in physics and engineering of the quantum dots, including successful development of quantum dot lasers. Prospect of future photonic devices based on the the quantum dots is also discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization of TiO2 composite coating on pc-WLED package to enhance optical efficiency
abstract: Enhancement of optical efficiency and angular color temperature deviation was studied with TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> composite coating on white LED package. By optimizing the curvature of TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> composite coating, the optical power from the pc-WLED package was enhanced 40% and the angular deviation of color correlation temperature was also improved.

articleTitle: Dynamic observation of laser-tissue interaction with optical coherence tomography
abstract: We propose to use optical coherence tomography (OCT) to evaluate the interaction between laser and biological tissue. The developed OCT system enables to achieve 3D structural and microcirculation imaging. The results show that OCT could be a potential tool for guidance of laser surgery to effectively improve the treatment efficiency.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of polarization beam splitter based on auto-cloning photonic crystal
abstract: Polarization beam splitter is realized by arraying small half-wave plates having different principal axis directions. We monolithically fabricated it that operates in optical communication wavelength by using auto-cloning photonic crystal. Large separation angle of 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> and low insertion loss of 0.9 dB are obtained.

articleTitle: Consideration of equilibrium condition in Shockley-Queisser limit for solar cell efficiency
abstract: The limit of solar cell efficiency reported by Shockley and Queisser has been considered by taking the material parameters based on the Fermi-Dirac statistics into account, and by introducing the nonradiative lifetime as a parameter. A practical limit of conversion efficiency and its bandgap dependence have been made clear.

articleTitle: Recent advances in nanoscale photonic MEMS
abstract: The combination of micro-electro-mechanical-system (MEMS) actuation and silicon photonics offers a powerful platform for integrating large-scale reconfigurable/tunable photonic systems. In this paper, we review the recent advances in silicon photonic MEMS and present detailed results of tunable microdisk filters and large-scale integrated photonic switches.

articleTitle: Fabrication of fine metal structure by using interference pattern of copropagating optical vortices and lift-off process
abstract: To fabricate fine metal structure, we proposed and demonstrated a method by using interference pattern of copropagating optical vortices and lift-off process. This method can fabricate more fine structure compared with the conventional laser drawing method using Gaussian beam even if the low numerical aperture condition.

articleTitle: Pump phase-locking to phase-conjugated twin waves with heterodyne OPLL assisted by sum-frequency and second harmonic generation for ND-PSAs
abstract: Heterodyne optical phase-locked loop assisted by sum-frequency and second-harmonic generation for non-degenerate phase-sensitive optical amplifier repeaters is proposed. Experiment of offset pump phase-locking to 5-Gbit/s BPSK phase-conjugated twin waves is successfully achieved by our method.

articleTitle: Multicast wavelength allocation for energy-efficient access networks considering wavelength switching time of T-band devices
abstract: The broad wavelength range of T-band has been developed as a new optical communication wavelength band. However, long wavelength switching time is an issue in wavelength routing. We propose a multicast wavelength allocation method taking the wavelength switching time into account for energy-efficient access networks.

articleTitle: Phase effect on silicon-wire based broadband directional coupler using Mach-Zehnder structure for CWDM applications
abstract: A Mach-Zehnder directional coupler (MZDC) is utilized to match the maximal flatness in wavelength and different coupling ratio for course wavelength division multiplexing. Here, the phase from MZDC bend structures on a 250-nm thick silicon-wire is analyzed and will significantly degrade the wavelength flatness and extinction ratio without appropriate compensation.

articleTitle: Magneto-plasmonics on perpendicular magnetic nanostructures consisting of CoPt layers and noble metal grains
abstract: The magneto-optical (MO) properties of perpendicular magnetic nanostructures consisting of CoPt layers and isolated fine grains of Ag or Au were investigated. The nanostructures exhibited a polarization reversal on Kerr rotation, and the Kerr loop depended on the external environment. These MO behaviors are attributed to localized plasmon resonance.

articleTitle: Transient absorption of titanium dioxide sputtered film deposited on two-dimensionally assembled gold nanoparticles
abstract: Two-layer film of titanium dioxide and gold nanoparticles was deposited onto glass substrate, and its extinction spectrum and transient absorption were measured. The gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were deposited on silane-treated glass by wet process, which showed enhancement of optical absorption due to its surface plasmon resonance (SPR). On the AuNP self-assembly, the titanium dioxide was deposited by magnetron sputtering. The absorption spectra in the region of 400-600 nm suggested that the red-shift of plasmon band of the AuNP due to surrounding in the TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> film. Transient absorption study proved that the lifetime of the conductive electrons depended on the film thickness the of titanium dioxide layer.

articleTitle: Asymmetric LP01-LP11-LP01 mode conversion along in-line few-mode fibers for all-fiber bandpass filters
abstract: We study the modal conversion and propagation properties of LP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode in graded-index and step-index few-mode fibers. An all-fiber bandpass filter is demonstrated by applying rotatable and variable long-period fiber gratings to the two consecutive few-mode fibers.

articleTitle: Fabrication of micro-tip for coupling to wire waveguides
abstract: There is a problem of dimensional mismatch in the connection from the optical fiber to the wire waveguide. We fabricated micro-tip with light curable resin at the optical fiber edge. The emitted light from the fiber was collected by the micro-tip, and the spot size became several microns.

articleTitle: Imaging of topologically protected elastic mode in silica 1D phononic crystal via photoelastic effect
abstract: We measure the spatial distribution of a topologically protected elastic modes in a silica 1D phononic crystal (PnC) by using the photoelasticity imaging technique. The strong localization of the topological elastic mode at the interface of two-joined PnCs with topologically distinct bandgaps is experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Luminescence investigation of near white light emitting zinc stannate
abstract: We experimentally investigate the photoluminescence properties of undoped and Ti-doped Zn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>SnO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (ZTO) powders via a sol-gel process. The intrinsic luminescence of ZTO exhibits near white-light emission, under UV excitation at 327 nm. Significant enhancement in emission intensity was demonstrated for the doped phosphors.

articleTitle: Hybrid refractive-diffractive spectrum-splitting module as a full-spectrum concentrator
abstract: A spectrum-splitting module for separating the visible and infrared spectra is proposed. The proposed module consists of the hybrid refractive-diffractive optical arrays and a light-guide plate. Those side surfaces of light-guide plate can be connected to different receivers for different applications.

articleTitle: Compact structured-light projector for 3D surface profiling
abstract: We present a highly compact projector using a diffractive optical element (DOE) and a collimated laser beam to project light patterns on to a three-dimensional (3D) surface as used in structured-light 3D surface profilers. The compact device has been designed to work in a far-field range from 4 mm to 40 mm with the pattern size of 5 mm× 5 mm at 10 mm distance, yielding a projection angle of 28°. A first prototype successfully demonstrated projection of stripe patterns over this large depth-of-focus range with a very short image plane distance of 4 mm.

articleTitle: Numerical estimation of dispersion effect in deeply-etched fully integrated MEMS Mach-Zhender interferometer
abstract: In this paper we numerically investigate the impact of Silicon refractive index dispersion on white source interferometry of deeply etched Mach-Zhender interferometer. The numerical simulations show that the dispersion effect results in a chirped and shifted interferogram. The dispersed interferogram can be compensated by utilizing long travel range electrostatic MEMS actuators.

articleTitle: Biomimetic optical systems — Strategies for miniaturization of optics
abstract: Micro-optics is a well-established technology which is integrated in many industrial, medical and consumer products today. However, micro-optics will not follow the path of micro-electronics, where further miniaturization always triggered higher performance at lower costs. The scaling laws of optics and biomimetic strategies for miniaturization of optics will be discussed.

articleTitle: Opto-mechanical ferrule-top devices in life science research
abstract: Opto-mechanical ferrule-top devices offer life science researchers unprecedented opportunities to investigate the role of mechanics in the physiology of cells and tissues. This paper provides a brief review summarizing the main achievements in the field.

articleTitle: Optical-to-wireless media conversion by utilizing cross gain modulation at semiconductor optical amplifier
abstract: We devise an optical-to-wireless media conversion method by XGM at the SOA aiming for a future use at a THz-wave access. We investigate the XGM characteristics and the performance of our proposed media conversion method. We configure the media-converted data transmission system and demonstrate an error free transmission.

articleTitle: Novel measurement method for optical pulse width at high-repetition frequency
abstract: We propose a measurement method of the optical pulse width at high-repetition frequencies. It consists of simple components such as a self-delayed interferometer and an optical power meter. We generated 50-GHz repetition pulses by superposing several lightwaves with 50-GHz spacing, and measured their pulse width with this measurement system.

articleTitle: Effective permeability measurement of μ-negative metamaterials using an inductance method
abstract: An inductance method is proposed in the paper to measure the effective permeability of μ-negative metamaterials. The method is achieved by measuring the inductance response of a multiple coil inspired by exciting current and metamaterials. The theory, simulation model and results are presented and the performance is also discussed.

articleTitle: Real time sensing of 12CO2 and 13CO2 using 2μm DFB-LD
abstract: For precise study of volcano activity compact and in-situ CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> isotope abundance ratio is highly desirable. In this study, real time measurement of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup>CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup>CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> was achieved by wavelength modulation spectroscopy using 2 μm DFB-LD. Measurement of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> in the human breath and the atmosphere were successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Pressure dependence of Brillouin frequency shift in plastic optical fibers
abstract: We investigate the pressure dependence of the Brillouin frequency shift in plastic optical fibers, which shows hysteresis. The pressure-dependence coefficient (mitigated hysteresis) is +4.3 MHz/MPa, the absolute value of which is 5.8 times larger than that of bare silica fibers.

articleTitle: Experimental observation of depolarized GAWBS in partially uncoated optical fibre
abstract: We observed the depolarized guided acoustic-wave Brillouin scattering (GAWBS) spectrum in a highly nonlinear fibre with partially side-stripped polymer coating. The linewidth of the GAWBS spectral line at 941 MHz was measured to be 6.4 MHz, which was 0.9 times that of a coated fibre.

articleTitle: Sensing the Earth with micro-optics
abstract: We present a multiplexed quasi-static strain sensor system with sub-nano resolution based on the transient response of fiber Fabry-Perot interferometers. A 3-channel strain measurement with resolution better than 0.2 nϵ/√Hz in frequency band from 0.1 Hz to 100 Hz is realized in the demonstrational experiments.

articleTitle: Proposal of Si waveguide optical isolator based on nonreciprocal TE-TM mode conversion using magneto-optical phase shift for TM mode
abstract: A novel Si waveguide optical isolator is proposed based on the nonreciprocal TE-TM mode conversion using the magneto-optical phase shift for the TM mode. A maximum isolation of 31 dB is demonstrated at a wavelength of 1545 nm for the TM mode input.

articleTitle: Effect of UV irradiation on transmittance spectra in polymer stabilized cholesteric liquid crystals
abstract: The optical properties for polymer stabilized cholesteric liquid crystals (CLCs) by different UV irradiation conditions are investigated by the spectroscopic measurements at various temperatures. The experimental results show that the bandwidth of selective transmittance spectra in CLCs varies with the increase of temperature depending on the wavelength of light source and illumination conditions for polymerization.

articleTitle: Enhanced optical absorption in nanowires over a desire range of wavelengths
abstract: Engineering optical absorption in nanowires, over a desire range of wavelengths is of importance to design high-performance nanowire-based photovoltaics. To this end, we integrate the nanowires with distributed Bragg reflectors to enhance absorption spectra of the nanowires and relate the consequent enhancement to increasing the optical path lengths of the modes.

articleTitle: Numerical analyses of all-optical gate switches employing periodically poled lithium niobate devices: Pattern effect of domain length error
abstract: We calculate characteristics of all-optical gate switches using the PPLN devices with consideration for the domain length error. The error causes decrease in the output power. Variation of the error pattern changes the output waveform.

articleTitle: Observation of stimulated brillouin scattering growth along optical fiber using two-photon absorption process in a silicon avalanche photodiode
abstract: We investigated a simple method to observe the growth of stimulated Brillouin scattering along an optical fiber using two-photon absorption (TPA) process in a silicon avalanche photodiode. The principle is based on the fact that the TPA photocurrent is proportional to the intensity correlation between reference light and Stokes light.

articleTitle: Distance measurement using free space optics
abstract: In this work, free space optics (FOS) is used for short distance measurement between two points having laser source at one end and light detector at the other end. Change of light intensity with respect to distance has been considered for the measurement. A mathematical model has been established for the purpose neglecting atmospheric disturbance.

articleTitle: Small-signal response of slow-light VCSEL amplifier
abstract: Small-signal analysis of a slow-light VCSEL amplifier is introduced using a traveling-wave rate equations model. Theoretical calculations show that the small-signal optical modulation bandwidth of the slow-light mode has strong dependences on the slowdown factor and length of the amplifier; it can be boosted to more than 50 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of new azimuth-type lens for reading glasses with extended depth of focus
abstract: We proposed a lens for reading glasses based on a light sword optical element (LSOE) that was designed to eliminate discontinuity. The characteristics of the lens were evaluated assuming a simplified presbyopic eye model. The results show the extended depth of focus of the lens and the improved image quality compared with that for an LSOE at different viewing angles.

articleTitle: Perfluorinated graded-index plastic optical fiber Bragg gratings: Observation and theoretical analysis of unique dependence on pressure
abstract: The pressure dependence of a fiber Bragg grating (FBG) inscribed in a perfluorinated graded-index plastic optical fiber (POF) is investigated at 1550 nm. As pressure is applied, the Bragg wavelength shifts with a relatively long time constant (several tens of minutes) with a coefficient of 1.3 nm/MPa, which is over 5 times the highest value previously reported in other POF-FBGs). After the Bragg wavelength becomes constant at 0.5 MPa, the pressure-dependence coefficient is quickly measured to be −0.13 nm/MPa, the sign of which is opposite to those of other POF-FBGs. These unique behaviors are theoretically analyzed.

articleTitle: The application of micro laser Doppler velocimeter to hemodialysis
abstract: Accurate measurement of dialyzed blood flow velocity is an important medical procedure. We successfully measure absolute blood flow velocity by increasing laser power density and selecting the appropriate wavelength of a Laser Doppler Velocimeter (LDV). This enables accurate measurement of the velocity of high-concentration fluid.

articleTitle: Artifacts in fluorescence lifetime imaging of gold nanorod dimer
abstract: We model the artifacts arising in the fluorescence lifetime imaging of gold nanorod dimers. Taking the scanning probe as a dipole emitter, we calculate the environment-dependent Purcell factor and show how to distinguish artifacts from the real morphology.

articleTitle: Low-noise graded-index plastic optical fiber for consumer photonics in 8K era
abstract: We propose significantly low-noise graded-index plastic optical fibers (GI POFs) for consumer-friendly pluggable 8K optical interfaces. It is confirmed that the GI POFs with the specified microscopic heterogeneities achieve highly-stable and high-speed data transmission in a consumer optical link without optical isolators.

articleTitle: Evaluation of inverse tangent phase mask in wavefront coding
abstract: An inverse tangential phase mask (ITPM) is potentially effective for extending the depth of field in the wavefront coding method. However, its characteristics have not been reported in detail. In this study, we obtained the ITPM profile function and confirmed that the optimized ITPM is more effective than a cubic phase mask (CPM) in several respects.

articleTitle: Emission spectrum evaluation of 0.8–1.1 μm range chirped multiple quantum wells for optical sensing
abstract: 0.8-1.1 μm range broadband light source is needed for food and medical sensing applications. Several types of chirped quantum well structures were prepared by metal organic vapor epitaxy. In this paper, the emission spectra of PL and EL were compared and effect of stacking order was experimentally investigated.

articleTitle: Thermally annealed gold film on optical fiber for multimode interferometric refractive index measurement
abstract: A simple method to form gold nanoparticles was applied to a fiber-optic interferometer to measure the refractive index. To form nanoparticles on the fiber, sputter-deposited gold thin film was thermally annealed. The sensitivity was improved when combining the gold nanoparticles with the optical fiber-based multimode interference sensor.

articleTitle: Simultaneous utilization of spontaneous emission and laser emission in VCSEL for efficiency improvement of optical wireless power transmission
abstract: Optical wireless power transmission has various advantages. An important technical issue is system efficiency improvement. In this research, we propose to use both laser light and spontaneous emission light simultaneously for improvement of power conversion efficiency of a light source. Numerical simulation results are discussed.

articleTitle: Nanostructured gradient index microlens for mid infrared applications
abstract: We present a new concept for GRIN lens development which can be used for both near- and mid-infrared applications. Internal nanostructure allow to obtain lens with arbitrary refractive index distribution. Use of a pair of thermally matched glasses with high transmission in the infrared permits performance in broadband infrared range.

articleTitle: Three dimensional compressive strain and its effect on optical properties of GaN-based light emitting diode grown on patterned sapphire substrate by confocal spectromicroscopy
abstract: We performed depth-resolved spectral mappings of GaN-based LED and results showed that the strain distribution propagating from PSS-GaN heterointerface toward surface and the PL intensity are spatially correlated. Numerical simulation based on indium composition distribution led to a radiative recombination rate distribution shows agreement with the experimental PL intensity distribution.

articleTitle: Analysis on Si modified MMI-waveguide-type optical switch operated with carrier injection
abstract: Silicon modified multimode-interference(MMI)-waveguide-type 2×2 optical switch operated with carrier injection was proposed for efficient modulation by flattening the refractive index profile of the waveguide. Fundamental designing and switching characteristics were analyzed.

articleTitle: Design method of a liquid crystal based computer-generated hologram for freeform surface measurement
abstract: Computer-generated hologram (CGH) is an essential component for aspheric and freeform surface measurement in the interferometry. Traditionally, CGH is manufactured by photolithography which is costly and time-consuming. A novel liquid crystal CGH and the design method based on the birefringence properties of LC and photo-alignment technology is presented in this paper. Simulation shows that this is a simple and reliable CGH design method which is appropriate for freeform interferometry test.

articleTitle: Optical performance of computer generated hologram under a small reconstruction beam
abstract: In this paper, the far-field diffraction pattern of a CGH under a reconstruction beam with a beam area smaller than device area of CGH is investigated. A series of beam size is simulated. It is found that the contrast of diffraction pattern will be increased as an increasing area of the reconstruction beam.

articleTitle: Photonic crystal Fano lasers and Fano switches
abstract: We show that Fano resonances can be realized in photonic crystal membrane structures by coupling line-defect waveguides and point-defect nanocavities. The Fano resonance can be exploited to realize optical switches with very small switching energy, as well as Fano lasers, that can generate short optical pulses.

articleTitle: Gallium diffused lithium niobate optical waveguide
abstract: Single mode waveguide operating at 1550 nm wavelength has been fabricated in lithium niobate using gallium ions indiffusion. Extraordinary and ordinary refractive indices are increased supporting TM and TE modes, respectively, and the diffusivity of gallium is one order of magnitude higher than that of titanium.

articleTitle: Robust silicon 3-dB coupler using inverse engineering based optimization
abstract: We propose a scheme to optimize the adiabaticity of silicon 3-dB couplers for broadband operation. Using inverse engineering based optimization, a 125 μm long silicon 3-dB coupler with a maximum imbalance of 0.8 dB from 1.4 to 1.7 μm and good fabrication tolerance is obtained.

articleTitle: Diaphragm thickness-dependent sensitivity in a glass-based guided-wave optical microphone
abstract: Our original guided-wave optical microphone consists of a diaphragm and a single-mode optical waveguide. Sensitivity is an important specification for microphones, and is theoretically known to be dependent on diaphragm thickness. In this study, we fabricated three microphones with different diaphragm thicknesses, and experimentally examined the diaphragm thickness-dependent sensitivity.

articleTitle: Lasing characteristics of intermixed highly-stacked quantum dot structure by ion implantation for wavelength-manipulated light sources
abstract: We have developed the quantum dot intermixing (QDI) technique using ion implantation and rapid thermal annealing (RTA) on highly-stacked quantum dot (QD) structure for wavelength-manipulated light sources. We report lasing characteristics of QDI structure (QDI-LD) whose oscillation wavelengths were ranged from 1550nm to 1350 nm.

articleTitle: Surface functionalization by femtosecond lasers and its ultrafast formation dynamics
abstract: In this work, I will discuss a number of techniques developed in my lab that allow us to functionalize material surfaces through femtosecond laser processing. The techniques led to the creation of the so-called black and colored metals, brighter light sources, superhydrophillic and superhydrophobic surfaces. We will further discuss our recent work in recording surface structural dynamics through an ultrafast imaging technique.

articleTitle: The multifaceted world of photonic crystal fibres
abstract: Recent developments in photonic crystal fibres, covering fields as diverse as ultrabroadband supercontinuum generation, optomechanics and optoacoustics, orbital angular momentum, laser tweezers and nonlinear frequency conversion in gases, will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Proximity amplitude and phase control for beam reduction using computer-generated hologram
abstract: Design method of a computer-generated hologram for reduction of the focused beam size is demonstrated. The key points are an arrangement of parallel beams and a specific constraint of their phases and amplitudes in the iterative Fourier transform algorithm. The focused beam was reduced to 75% or less of the diffraction limit.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of adaptive gain control of quantum-dot SOA for unicast/multicast wavelength selective routing systems in T-band
abstract: Optical multicast routing is used for many applications such as video streaming and energy-efficient networking. We propose adaptive gain control of a quantum-dot-based semiconductor optical amplifier (QD-SOA) for optical unicast and multicast wavelength selective routing systems in T-band to compensate optical power loss according to the number of destination nodes.

articleTitle: Tolerance to lateral displacement and angular deflection on mode sorting performance for beams carrying orbital angular momentum
abstract: We numerically investigate the tolerance to lateral displacement and angular deflection on the mode sorting performances for beams carrying orbital angular momentum. Comparing Laguerre-Gaussian beams and perfect vortex beams in terms of crosstalk on the sorting result reveals that Laguerre-Gaussian beams show stronger tolerance.

articleTitle: Bragg grating coupled high Q factor ring resonator using LSCVD deposited Si3N4 film
abstract: High-quality Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> films with low optical loss were deposited at 150°C using LSCVD. A micro-ring resonator based on as-deposited Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> with Q-factor of 5.2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> has been demonstrated. Bragg gratings are fabricated at bus ends to improve coupling efficiency. The LSCVD deposited Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> exemplify its viability as a photonic integration platform.

articleTitle: Narrow-band plasmonic thermal emitter using plasmonic nanochannel structure
abstract: A plasmonic nanochannel structure consisting of periodic vertical Au/Si/Au nanochannels connected by U-shaped gold layers is demonstrated as a narrow-band plasmonic thermal emitter. Due to coupling of localized surface plasmons in the channels and propagating surface plasmons under the U-shaped gold layers, a narrow-band emission peak is observed.

articleTitle: Enhanced thermal stability of electro-optic polymer modulator
abstract: We synthesized the EO polymer having a glass transition temperature (Tg) higher than 190°C. The fabricated waveguide modulator was tested for the thermal and temporal stability at 105 °C for longer than 2000 hours. The EO activity of the measured polymer modulator is attributed to the high molecular hyperpolarizability of the used chromophores, and thermal stability to the high Tg of the EO polymer.

articleTitle: Thermoplasmonics of micro glassbead coated with gold nanoparticles
abstract: The micro glass bead, which were covered by gold nanoparticles, was fabricated by wet process and studied for the plasmonic nano heater in water. The plasmonic beads of > 3 μm in diameter were thermally treated with electric oven for 3 hours. The thermoplasmonic bead generated plasmonic bubbles by laser illumination of the wavelength of 473 nm and the power of 32 mW.

articleTitle: Quadrature imbalance compensation for M-ary modulated signals interleaved with reference light
abstract: We propose digital compensation method of quadrature imbalance for M-ary modulated signals interleaved with reference light. Error vector magnitude of 10-Gbaud interleaved QPSK signals with Quadrature imbalance is improved by 18.8 % under 18-dB SNR condition.

articleTitle: Efficiency evaluation of hybrid concentrated photovoltaic under direct and diffuse illumination
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized CPV system is experimentally demonstrated based on a hot embossing silicone lens array with a size of 2 cm × 2 cm. Owing to the small size of the lens array, the total track of the CPV system can be as small as 4 cm. Consquently, the weight of the CPV system can be much lower than conventional bulky CPV system. For harvesting the diffuse solar radiation, perovskite solar cells are mounted adjacent to III-V solar cell. Theoretically, the optical efficiency can be enhanced from 70 % to 76% for γ = 0.7 In the future, we will experimentally integrate III-V solar chip with perovskite solar cell to harvest both direct and diffuse solar light, respectively. The solar conversion efficiency will be discussed as well.

articleTitle: Waveguide-type optical circuit for recognition of 8PSK-coded labels
abstract: In photonic label routing nodes, recognition of optical labels is one of the key functions. In this paper, we propose an optical recognition circuit for 8-ary phase shift keying labels based on the previously reported waveguide circuit for optical label recognition in quadrature phase shift keying format.

articleTitle: Linewidth-adjustable silicon photonics waveguide Bragg filters
abstract: Linewidth-adjustable silicon waveguide filters are implemented by employing misaligned corrugations. This approach not only allows fine linewidth tuning of narrowband cladding-modulated waveguide filter but also enables dual-wavelength filtering with equal and narrow linewidth. We anticipate those devices can be applied for WDM or polarization-independent filter applications.

articleTitle: GaN-based vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers operating at high temperature
abstract: We report on GaN-based vertical-cavity surface emitting lasers (VCSELs) capable of high temperature operation. The structures of VCSELs include double dielectric distributed Bragg reflectors and bonded to a silicon substrate with a p-side-down configuration, allowing a better heat dissipation. The temperature dependent lasing characteristics of VCSELs can sustain to 350K.

articleTitle: Monolithic optical phased arrays in silicon
abstract: This paper covers a summary of recent developments, architectural choices, building blocks, and selected challenges in the area of monolithic silicon optical phased arrays with emphasis on imaging applications.

articleTitle: Light-emitting diode conditioned with YAG:Ce3+ phosphors and CdSe/ZnS quantum dots for high color-rendering-index white-light generation
abstract: By processing the blue LED light with properly combined yellow emissive YAG:Ce<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup> phosphors and red emissive CdSe/ZnS quantum dots, we are able to produce white light with a high color-rendering index of 95.4,an R9 value of 95.0, and a low correlated color temperature of 3640 K.

articleTitle: Metamaterial computational ghost imaging
abstract: A novel metamaterial computational ghost imaging (MCGI) is presented in this paper. Due to the properties of metamaterials, it can provide special feature which SLM or DMD does not have. Metamaterials can also be used in other bands which plays a positive role in extending the application of ghost imaging.

articleTitle: Fabrication and characterization of a binary diffractive lens for controlling the focal length and depth of focus
abstract: We report on the fabrication and analysis of a diffractive lens with binary structure that allows the control of focal length and depth of focus. Beam propagation measurements show that focal length and depth of focus depend upon the structural parameters of prototype lenses.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional all-fluidic imaging systems
abstract: Employing the cylindrical geometry of classical optical systems combined with complex microfabricated electrode configurations, three dimensional all-fluidic components are fabricated inside a tube and combined to yield multi-component optical systems. Tunable lenses; tiltable and rotatable prisms; aberration-tunable lenses; variable apertures; and a complete multi-lens zoom system are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Resistance evaluation of holographic polymer-dispersed liquid crystal memory for gamma-ray irradiation
abstract: The radiation-hardened characteristics of holographic polymer-dispersed liquid crystal (HPDLC) memory are investigated for the applications requiring high reliability using an optically reconfigurable gate array. The optical properties and internal grating structures are investigated by using a cobalt 60 gamma radiation source to examine the resistance of 100 Mrad total-ionizing-dose.

articleTitle: Vertical split-ring resonator metamaterial for isotropic absorption and sensor
abstract: The four VSRRs are combined an isotropic perfect absorber which is independent to the polarization orientation and angle of incidences. Furthermore, it can also be a refractive index sensor with significant improvment of sensing performance.

articleTitle: Enlarging acceptance angle of a planar solar concentrator with a v-groove array
abstract: The acceptance angle and the optical efficiency of a planar solar concentrator with v-groove array were studied in this article. In simulation, the acceptance angle was enlarged from 2° to 4.5°, while the discrepancy between the simulated and measured optical efficiencies of the concentrator was investigated.

articleTitle: Optimizing the design of trefoil phase plates for wavefront coding
abstract: Wavefront Coding (WFC) is a technique which makes use of generalized aspheric optics and digital signal processing to greatly increase the depth of focus and/or reduce the cost of imaging systems. Usually, cubic phase elements are employed to obtain images that are insensitive to defocus and some aberrations. In this work we will show how to optimize the design of a trefoil phase plate in order to optimize its performance for large amounts of defocus.

articleTitle: Analysis of phase-sensitive amplification in phase-shifted periodically-poled waveguide for discrimination and amplification of optical vector modulation signal
abstract: We propose discrimination and amplification device using phase sensitive amplification based on the second order nonlinear optical effects in phase-shifted periodically polled lithium niobate waveguides. The amplification characteristics in phase-shifted periodically polled structures were analysed by using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method.

articleTitle: Electro-optic spatial light modulator/deflector using multi-stage polarization-reversed structure
abstract: We have proposed a new electro-optic Bragg-diffraction type spatial modulator/deflector using multi-stage polarization-reversed structures, which can deflect a laser beam with a high speed over GHz. In this paper, the operational principle and deflection characteristics of the proto-type device are reported.

articleTitle: Proposal of compact three-mode exchanger based on symmetric and asymmetric directional couplers with integrated mode rotator
abstract: A compact three-mode exchanger composed of symmetric/asymmetric directional couplers with mode rotators is proposed for mode-division-multiplexing system. Compared with previously proposed device, the footprint of the chip is 75% and the number of directional couplers and rotators is half by using the coupling length difference between LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> and LP<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11b</sub> modes.

articleTitle: Optical and emission properties of dye molecules captured in the mesoscale channels of micron-sized metal-organic framework crystals
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks with pre-organized channels can be utilized to host various dye molecules to control their optical properties. The anionic framework of In-BTB MOF is an ideal host for encapsulating Reichardt's dye and rhodamine 6G. The optical properties of both encapsulated dyes were investigated using solid-state UV/Vis and fluorescence spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Metasurface-based ultra-thin circular polarization analyzer integrated with semiconductor photodetectors
abstract: We report on a metal-dielectric-metal (MDM) waveguide-based circular polarization analyzer with a sub-micron-scale thickness. By integrating nano-aperture metasurface and semiconductor photodetectors with the MDM structure, we can discriminate the handedness of circularly polarized light directly from the photocurrents without the usage of conventional optical components.

articleTitle: Compensation of optical aberration for improvement of image quality in virtual-phase-conjugation based optical tomography
abstract: We propose virtual-phase-conjugation based optical tomography (VPC-OT) incorporated with the compensation of the optical aberration for improving the imaging quality. The compensation scheme is implemented by optically measuring the transmission function of the beam propagation. Then, we confirmed that this scheme greatly improves the signal level of VPC-OT.

articleTitle: Pattern effects of random domain length error in PPLN-based all-optical retiming switches
abstract: We calculate switching performance of all-optical retiming switches employing the cascade of second harmonic generation and difference frequency mixing in the PPLN devices with consideration for the random domain length error. The error decreases the output power. The difference of the error pattern varies the waveform and the signal quality of the output.

articleTitle: Detection of world's shortest hot spots in silica and plastic optical fibers by slope-assisted brillouin optical correlation-domain reflectometry
abstract: Based on the “beyond-nominal-resolution” effect of slope-assisted Brillouin optical correlation-domain reflectometry, we demonstrate the detections of shortest-ever hot spots. A 2-mm-long strained section in a silica single-mode fiber and a 5-mm-long heated section in a plastic optical fiber are correctly detected in a distributed manner.

articleTitle: Pre-distortion technique for compensating QAM signal distortions generated by dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulators with low-extinction ratio and small-chirp parameter
abstract: We propose a pre-distortion method in the electrical domain to compensate for IQ-distortion that is attributed to some imbalances of dual-parallel Mach-Zehnder modulators for optical QAM. We confirmed the effect of the method by performing calculations, and the calculation results show the potential to improve the signal quality.

articleTitle: List of MOC2017 committee members
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members and society officers.

articleTitle: 30 Years of Microoptics Conference
abstract: The 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> Microoptics Conference (MOC) was held in Tokyo on October 15–16, 1987. Since then, MOC is held every odd-numbered year in Japan sponsored by The Japan Society of Applied Physics (JSAP). From 2004, for possible even-numbered years, MOC has been held outside of Japan. Some MOCs were jointed or co-located with other conferences. In my today's talk, general and topical trends on microoptics for the past three decades are reviewed.
